verbalization: Zeylanol appears to have multiple targets that ultimately lead to Riboflavin synthase through a series of molecular interactions. The evidence suggests that Zeylanol may act as a modulator of a voltage-dependent T-type calcium channel subunit, which is targeted by Azadirachtin Q and Eucalyptus gum. These compounds, in turn, target Riboflavin synthase, indicating a potential pathway where Zeylanol could influence the activity of these calcium channels, which may in turn affect the synthesis of riboflavin. The presence of multiple targets and their shared downstream effect on Riboflavin synthase suggests a possible regulatory mechanism involving calcium signaling or other cellular processes that are indirectly linked to riboflavin biosynthesis. The integration of these pathways highlights the complexity of the relationship between Zeylanol and Riboflavin synthase, emphasizing the role of calcium channels in mediating this interaction.
